correctness.rationale: With nonempty A, the quantity t+(1−e)+(1−f) counts T augmented by ∅ and A. It is 2 on the singleton; an empty-parameter factor changes neither the augmented family nor m. For both factors nonempty in parameters, a union can duplicate only ∅ and necessarily misses A; the augmented count is t_1+t_2+2−e_1−e_2, at most the sum of the two child augmented counts. For a join the roles are swapped: only A can be duplicated, ∅ is absent, and the count is t_1+t_2+2−f_1−f_2. The resulting induction proves the bound for all finite cographs. Each leaf twin realizes its singleton; each internal apex realizes its descendant leaf set, all distinct by full binary branching; an isolate realizes ∅. There are exactly 2m external witnesses and m parameters, including the edge-plus-isolate case m=1. No host with fewer than 3m vertices can provide the 2m separate external witnesses. All-vertex adjacency traces are not all complete equality-sensitive quantifier-free types, a distinction correctly made in the stated scope. The uploaded finite checks were read, not run; the proof does not depend on them.
residual_risks: No all-vertex equality-sensitive type bound or bound for formulas of positive quantifier rank is certified.

evidence: Cographs are exactly the zero-twin-width graphs. The published general twin-width neighborhood bound is (d+2)2^(d+1)m, giving 4m at d=0, not 2m.

The fixed length and quantifier rank type result is polynomial rather than this exact coefficient. The sharp forest closed-neighborhood result cited in the comparison is ⌊7m/3⌋ for a different host class.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These broader literature results do not dominate the exact claim. The exact stronger coverage comes instead from the all-vertex open and closed spectra theorem and the standard cograph operations.

evidence: Start from its open 2m-vertex extremizer with m parameters. In a union/join construction replace the singleton leaf of each parameter a by an independent pair a,a′ with a′ kept external. This replaces only the leaf expression and so preserves the cograph property. It creates one external false twin per parameter and does not change A.

Every old external trace remains; every trace formerly witnessed by a∈A is witnessed by a′. Thus there are at least 2m distinct external traces; the all-vertex bound gives equality. The new host has 3m vertices, which is also the trivial witness-count lower bound. This argument works even at m=1.

The frozen all-vertex theorem and stronger penalty lemma are already literal statements there. Neither a different pictured extremizer nor same-day dating separates the claims mathematically.

evidence: The spectra record defines the same all-vertex open T and proves |T∪{∅,A}|≤2m. For m≥1 the added sets are distinct, so this is literally the frozen strengthened inequality.
